fields.meaning: Because… (that's why)…
fields.connection: V/A plain form + んだもん（spoken language, giving a reason）
examples: I'm not going today. I'm tired, okay?
I'm not crying. I just got something in my eye.
Sorry I'm late. The train was delayed, that's why.
So what? I wanted it, okay?
I'm a beginner, you know.
fields.explain:
Used in casual conversation; avoid it in formal speech or with superiors (except “～んですもの”).
Expresses emotion, sometimes in a childish way; suitable for explaining personal, minor reasons.
Can be combined with “だって” at the beginning of a sentence to emphasize the reason: だって、忙しい んだもん。

- Gives an emotional, casual reason or excuse: “because…”, “it's just that…”.
- Nuance: whiny, defensive, making excuses; often used by women/children, or when the speaker wants to downplay their responsibility.
- Usually comes at the end of a sentence; rarely followed by another clause.
fields.notes:
• “もん” is the spoken form of “もの”; “～んだもの” sounds more polite than “～んだもん”.
• When emphasizing annoyance: ～んだもん！ (rising intonation at the end of the sentence).
• In a dialogue, the previous sentence is often a question or reproach; the reply uses ～んだもん to justify oneself. explain: Used to explain a reason with an unhappy, annoyed or disappointed feeling
Common in casual speech ⏐ examples: 1. 「どうして食べないの？」「だって、まずいんだもん。」
“Why aren't you eating?” “Because it tastes awful, that's why.”
2. 今日の試験、できなかった・・・。勉強しなかったんだもん、仕方がない。
I couldn't do today's exam… well, I didn't study, so there's nothing I can do about it.
mistakes: Using it with superiors or in formal writing: inappropriate. Switch to ～ので／～から／～んです.
Forgetting “な” with N/na: 便利んだもん × correct: 便利なんだもん。
Confusing its nuance with ～から: the JLPT sets traps with options that do or do not carry a whiny, emotional nuance.

rows: <ruby>忙<rt>いそが</rt></ruby>しいから<ruby>行<rt>い</rt></ruby>けない。
Neutral; adding “もの” gives a softer nuance

fields.meaning: Instead, in exchange (sentence-initial conjunction)
examples: Please work overtime today. In exchange, you can go home early tomorrow.
My older brother isn't good at studying. Instead, he's good at sports.
This restaurant is expensive. In return, the taste is guaranteed.
fields.explain: A sentence-initial conjunction: it takes the whole first clause as the premise, and the second clause states something that replaces or compensates for it to an equal degree. In meaning it corresponds to ～かわりに, but it stands on its own at the beginning of the following sentence, usually followed by 「、」.

fields.name: ～ことだ（advice）
fields.meaning: That is to say; you should
examples: Keep warm and get plenty of rest.
You shouldn't overdo it.
fields.explain: Used when giving advice about something

fields.name: ～ますように（praying for）
fields.meaning: So that; hoping, praying for
fields.connection: Vます・Vません・Vれます + ように（praying for）
examples: I hope I pass.
I pray my mother recovers from her illness.
I hope I don't catch the flu.
fields.explain: Usually used to express hope or a prayer for something

fields.meaning: Not even a little, not at all
examples: I can't understand that person's English at all.
I don't worry about my figure at all.
I can only speak a little Japanese.
fields.explain: Used to emphasize the negative

fields.meaning: …is…, but…
examples: As for the piano, I can play it, but I'm not good at it.
This bag is expensive, sure, but it's really easy to use.
fields.explain: Used when you want to explain or state that the reality is lower, not to the degree the other person thinks

fields.meaning: About…
examples: To study Japanese culture.
To read "Notes on Taking the Entrance Exam."
fields.explain: Used when talking about an action or matter focused on a certain topic

fields.name: ～ように（desired result）
fields.meaning: Do… / Do not do…
examples: Do not smoke here.

"Come earlier tomorrow."
"Understood."
fields.explain: Used to request or instruct another person (of lower status) to do something

fields.name: ～まで（until）
fields.meaning: Until (an action)
examples: There are 30 minutes until the movie starts.
I'll be waiting until I hear from you.
fields.explain: Used to describe the end point of something

fields.name: ～らしい（typical）
fields.meaning: Like (manly, feminine, childish…)
examples: Today was a warm, spring-like day.
I don't often wear feminine clothes.
fields.explain: Used in spoken language. Used when you want to describe a characteristic you sense in a thing or situation

fields.name: ～とく・どく（contracted Vておく）
fields.meaning: Do something in advance, do something beforehand
examples: I'll write down in my notebook the parts I got wrong on the test.
Wash this for me, will you?
We're almost out of toilet paper, so I need to buy some.
fields.explain:
This is the contracted form of Vておく.
Vておく has 3 meanings:
Preparing something in advance. Taking care of a task. Leaving things as they are.
See also the grammar points that use Vておく: See

fields.name: ～(ら)れている（passive）
fields.meaning: Be done (passive)
examples: This book does not contain a detailed explanation.
The entrance ceremony will be held in this hall.
This is said to be the largest diamond in the world.
In the past, that idea was believed to be correct.
fields.explain:
Used to report something that is done by another agent (the agent is hidden)
Talks about things that are widely known.
See also:
Review the conjugation of verbs in the passive form (受身形）：See
Review the grammar points that use the passive form (受身形）：See

fields.name: ～上げる・～上がる（completion）
fields.meaning: Finish doing…
examples: I finally finished writing the report.
The cake has finished baking.
fields.explain: Used to talk about completely finishing or ending a task. Can be used with both intransitive and transitive verbs
fields.notes: Distinguish it from あげる for giving and receiving (the ～上げる line)

fields.meaning: Tell (someone), ask (someone) to do / not to do something
examples: Please tell Tanaka to come to my room.
My wife has told me not to smoke at home.
fields.explain:
Used when you want to ask someone to pass on your command to a third party
Or used when relaying a command passed on by someone else

fields.name: ～たところ（result・discovery）
fields.meaning: After trying to do something…
examples: When I asked the teacher what the next test would cover, I was told it goes up to Lesson 10.
My tooth hurt, so I went to the dentist, and I was told I had a bad cavity.
fields.explain: Used when you want to talk about surprise or the seriousness of a problem after trying to do something

fields.meaning: So that, in order to
examples: Please speak in a louder voice so that everyone can hear.
I'll write it in my planner so I don't forget.

I'm saving money to buy a house.
I quit school to work.
fields.explain:
Used to indicate the purpose of the action performed afterward
Cannot be used with transitive verbs or verbs expressing deliberate action. Usually used with verbs in the potential form or intransitive verbs

fields.meaning: Intended to do / not to do something
examples: I was planning to go shopping yesterday, but I had a headache, so I stayed home the whole time.
I meant not to eat any sweets, but I ended up eating some anyway.
fields.explain: Used to talk about a plan or intention to do something in the past that was not carried out afterward

fields.meaning: Want someone to do / not to do something for you
examples: Um, I'd like you to show me the textbook...
There's something I'd like you to teach me.
fields.explain: Used when you want to ask someone to do something for you; usually used in the plain form, not formal

fields.meaning:
最後まで～し続ける
Do ~ to the end
fields.connection: Vます(drop ます) + 通す (やり通す・読み通す)
examples: Let's see through to the end what we decided ourselves.
No matter what he was asked, he stayed silent throughout.
fields.notes: Attaches to verbs expressing a volitional action and expresses the meaning 「最後まで－．する」 (do all the way to the end). (316)

fields.meaning: Apparently, it means that, the fact is
fields.connection: V plain form + ということだ とのことだ / N + (だ) / Na + (だ) / Aい
examples: Tanaka called, and he says he'll be a little late.
The exam result was 70%, which means a pass.
fields.explain:
Has 2 main meanings:
– Reporting something heard or read
– Stating a meaning, fact or result that is drawn
The verb can be in the volitional or imperative form

fields.meaning:
「～の状態が続いているとき、ずっと…する・ずっと…の状態だ。」～は継続的なことを表す言葉。…継続的なことを表す文。
While state ~ continues, state … is carried out / takes place throughout that time.
~ is a word expressing something that continues over a certain period of time.
… is also a sentence expressing something that continues over a certain period of time.
「～の状態が続いているとき、 …する・…が起こる。」 ～は継続的なことを表す言葉。…は瞬間的なことを表す文。
While state ~ continues, … is done / … happens.
~ is a word expressing something that continues over a certain period of time.
… is a sentence expressing something that happens in a short moment.
fields.connection: Vている/Vる/Vない/Nの + 間、…（throughout the period）/ 間に、…（at a point within the period）
examples: While their mother was taking a nap, the children were watching TV.
Could you possibly take care of our dog while I'm away on a trip?
While their mother was taking a nap, the children went out to play.
While I was away on a trip, a lot of weeds grew in the garden.

fields.name: ～の（nominalization）
fields.meaning: The act of (noun)
fields.connection: V/Aい plain form + の / Na + な + の（nominalization: いいのを、元気なのが…）
examples: I completely forgot to call Tanaka.
I don't really like going to crowded places on Sundays.
fields.explain:
Used to turn nouns, verbs, adjectives and phrases into a noun phrase
Used in casual, concise contexts

fields.meaning: (Verb) all the way… / can't… all; do completely, thoroughly
examples: There's so much rice that I can't eat it all.
I read the long novel all the way through in two days.
Looking completely exhausted.
fields.explain:
Used when using up something completely, with nothing left over
Conversely, the negative form expresses that the action does not end, or that the action or quality of something goes on
fields.notes:
meaning_vi: Do to the finish, completely finish ⏐ examples: 1. この小説はおもしろくて、１日で読み切った。
This novel was so interesting that I read it all in one day.
2. 彼は疲れ切った顔をしている。
He looks completely exhausted.

fields.meaning: Be told / be warned / be scolded / be yelled at to do / not to do something
fields.connection: V imperative form・Vるな + と + 言われる・注意される・しかられる・怒られる
examples: The doctor told me not to drink alcohol.
My teacher told me to study harder.
My father warned me to come home earlier.
fields.explain: Used when reporting a command someone else gave you

fields.name: ～まで（even）
fields.meaning: To the extent of (noun), even
examples: You can eat this fish, bones and all.
Even you doubt me?
fields.explain: Used to express surprise at how great or excessive something is

fields.meaning: Asking permission to do something yourself.
fields.connection: V causative form て + ほしい
examples: I'd like you to let me rest.
Please do let me handle this job.
Yesterday I appealed to the section chief to let me work on the new project.
I have a headache, so I'd like to take the day off work today, if that's all right.

fields.meaning:
「passive」＋「causative」(使役受身) Expresses an unpleasant feeling when you end up in an unwanted situation because of someone's actions or words. Can also express a feeling brought about by some occasion.
【「～される／～（さ）せられる」の作り方】
読まない+　される／せられる→読まされる／読ませられる
見ない+　させられる→見させられる
こない+　させられる→こさせられる
する→させられる
fields.connection: Vる → V causative-passive form (待つ→待たされる; group II: 見る→見させられる)
examples: To be made to wait
I was made to listen to my older brother's terrible singing.
When I was a child, I was made to clean my room every day.
That movie made me realize how frightening war is.
Listening to my teacher's lecture made me think about environmental issues.
fields.explain:
「受身」＋「使役」Expresses an unpleasant feeling when you end up in an unwanted situation because of someone's actions or words. Can also express a feeling brought about by some occasion.
【「～される／～（さ）せられる」の作り方】
V-u：読まない+　される／せられる→読まされる／読ませられる
V-ru：見ない+　させられる→見させられる
V-irr（不規則）：こない+　させられる→こさせられる
する→させられる

fields.meaning:
「～という情報を受けて、…。」～はほかの人の話や様子などから分かったこと、…は話者の判断・意志・相手への働きかけの文など。
On receiving information ~ , …
~ is something the speaker has learned from what someone else said or from the actual situation.
… is a sentence expressing the speaker's judgment or intention, or urging the listener to do something.
fields.connection: V/A plain form + (の)なら / N/Na + なら（receiving information, then making a judgment）
examples: You're not using that box anymore? If you're not using it, please give it to me.
Oh, it's going to rain tomorrow? If it rains, it doesn't look like we'll be able to go cycling.
That book—if you've finished reading it, could you lend it to me?

fields.meaning: Every…, once every… (Nごとに)
examples: Please take this medicine every 6 hours.
The Olympics are held every 4 years.
Everyone I meet asks me the same question.

fields.meaning: …together, …each other (Vます+合う)
examples: Let's help each other when we're in trouble.
The two of them talked together about the future.
Don't hold back; please share your opinions with each other.

fields.meaning: Does nothing but… (negative description, ばかりで…ない)
fields.connection: V plain form + ばかりで / Na / Aい
examples: He does nothing but complain and never does anything.
This job is nothing but hard work, and the pay is low.
My son does nothing but play games and won't help me.

fields.meaning: Not particularly…, not especially… (別に～ない)
examples: I don't have anything in particular to do.
That movie wasn't particularly interesting.

A: Are you mad?
B: No, I'm not particularly mad.

fields.meaning: For the first time in (period of time)… (3年ぶりに)
fields.connection: [period of time] + ぶりに (3年ぶりに)
examples: I met my high school friends for the first time in 10 years.
The rain stopped for the first time in 3 days.
I ate food from my home country for the first time in a month.

fields.meaning: In the middle of…, throughout… (N中: ちゅう/じゅう)
examples: I'm in a meeting, so I'll call you back later.
Please submit the report by the end of today.
I worked part-time throughout the summer vacation.

fields.meaning: …or something (N か何か)
examples: I'm thirsty, so I'd like to drink some tea or something.
Do you have a pen or something to write with?
Would you like to go see a movie or something this weekend?

fields.meaning: In the end, after all…
examples: I thought about it a lot, but in the end I decided not to go.
In the end, nothing was decided at the meeting.
I hurried there, but in the end I didn't make it in time.

fields.meaning: …intently / deeply; …into (Vます+込む)
examples: Please don't jump into the river.
He is silent, lost in thought.
A stranger got into the house.

fields.meaning: Perhaps…, maybe… (もしかしたら～かもしれない)
fields.connection: もしかしたら もしかすると + [sentence/clause] + かもしれない
examples: It might snow tomorrow.
Maybe he has already gone home.
I might be able to go to Japan next month.

fields.meaning: If…, supposing… then (もしも～たら)
examples: If I won the lottery, I'd want to travel around the world.
If it rains tomorrow, the game will be canceled.
If you ever have any trouble, please contact me anytime.

fields.meaning: Re-… (do again one more time: Vます+直す)
examples: I rewrote the mistakes in my composition.
Please reconsider it once more.
I can't hear you well, so I'll call you back.
